userStories.title: Add vocal and instrument isolation from samples
userStories.description: As a sampler user, I want to isolate a vocal or instrument from a mixed sample so that I can audition and use that stem independently in a patch.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend: expose the available isolation targets, including vocals, and accept a supported mono or stereo source sample, an optional selected region, and the requested target stem.

Backend: a successful separation returns a playable derived sample with source identity, sample rate, channel count and duration metadata; the result stays aligned to the source region and the original sample remains unchanged.
Backend: separation runs without blocking audio playback and reports job progress, completion, cancellation and actionable failures; cancelling a job does not apply a result.
Backend: a result from a cancelled job or a source/patch that has since changed cannot silently alter the current sample or patch.

Frontend: the sample editor lets the user choose the whole sample or a region, select an available stem, start or cancel isolation, and see progress; unavailable targets and failed jobs show a clear reason and allow recovery without losing the original sample.
Frontend: after separation, the user can audition the original and isolated stem at matching sample positions before accepting or discarding the result.
Frontend and backend: accepting a stem adds a separate sample asset usable in the patch, preserves the original, survives patch save/reload, and supports undo back to the previous sample selection.
userStories.notes: P2 (normal). Backend requirements: source separation, discoverable target capabilities, asynchronous job lifecycle, aligned derived audio and metadata, cancellation/stale-result handling, and persistent sample assets. Frontend requirements: a sample-editor isolation action, source/region and stem selection, progress/cancel/error states, original-versus-result audition, and explicit accept/discard with undo. Example: extract a vocal from a mixed music sample and use it as a new sample in the current patch. Plan any missing engine/host separation and asset capabilities together with the bridge and React controls. Separation must stay outside the realtime audio path. Model/runtime choice, local versus remote execution, additional supported stems, resource limits and acceptable quality/latency remain planning decisions; no vendor or implementation is selected by this task.
